facts.claim: Philippine Airlines will operate its first-ever nonstop passenger flight from Manila (MNL) to Chicago O'Hare (ORD) on Monday, November 9, 2026, three times a week on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, using the Airbus A350-900.

Flight PR132 is scheduled to depart Manila at 4:40 p.m. with a block time of 14 hours 15 minutes, arriving Chicago at 4:55 p.m.; return flight PR133 departs Chicago at 10:45 p.m. with a block time of 16 hours 40 minutes, arriving Manila at 5:25 a.m. the next day.
The route was announced in April with limited-time round-trip basic economy fares of $667 for bookings until May 31; Cirium data shows year-round operation with a peak of 14 departures in March 2027.
The A350-900 on the route seats 295 in three classes: 30 business, 24 premium economy and 241 economy, with a 3-3-3 economy layout.

Chicago is Philippine Airlines' fifth US mainland destination after Los Angeles, New York JFK, San Francisco and Seattle-Tacoma, and its eighth US city overall including Guam, Honolulu and Saipan, the last served by PAL Express.

zh.title: 菲律賓航空首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛：西向回程近17小時，每週3班A350執飛
zh.summary: 菲律賓航空11月9日首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛航線，每週3班、由A350-900執飛；西向回程表定16小時40分，是該公司迄今最長的美國航線，美國航點增至8個。
body: 菲律賓航空將於11月9日（週一）首開馬尼拉尼諾伊·艾奎諾國際機場直飛芝加哥歐海爾國際機場的客運航線，每週3班、逢週一、週三、週五對開，由空中巴士A350-900執飛。這是該公司首條馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛航線，開航後美國航點增至8個，其中美國本土5個。

去程PR132班機預定馬尼拉時間16時40分出發，飛行14小時15分後於芝加哥時間16時55分抵達；回程PR133班機預定芝加哥時間22時45分出發，受西向強勁逆風影響，表定飛行16小時40分、翌日清晨5時25分抵達馬尼拉，清晨抵達有助旅客轉接菲律賓國內與亞洲區域航線。航線於4月宣布時，菲律賓航空曾推出667美元限時來回基本經濟艙票價，訂位期限至5月31日；依Cirium排班資料，航線全年營運，2027年3月為班次高峰、每月14班。

執飛機型為295席的A350-900，採三艙等配置：商務艙30席、特選經濟艙24席、經濟艙241席，經濟艙為每排9席的3-3-3配置。芝加哥是菲律賓航空在美國本土的第5個航點，其餘4個為洛杉磯、紐約甘迺迪、舊金山與西雅圖—塔科馬；加上關島、檀香山與塞班共3個美國非本土航點，其中塞班航線由區域品牌菲律賓航空快運（PAL Express）營運。菲律賓航空總裁納托爾（Richard Nuttall）表示，芝加哥—馬尼拉走廊將透過馬尼拉樞紐連結菲律賓國內主要市場與區域航點，並為美國中西部帶來直飛連結。

en.title: Philippine Airlines launches first nonstop Manila–Chicago service: near-17-hour westbound leg, three weekly A350 flights
en.summary: Philippine Airlines launches its first nonstop Manila–Chicago passenger service on November 9, operating three times a week with the Airbus A350-900; the westbound return is scheduled at 16 hours 40 minutes, making it the carrier's longest US route and lifting its US network to eight cities.
body: Philippine Airlines will operate its first-ever nonstop passenger flight from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) on Monday, November 9. The service will run three times a week, on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays in both directions, using the Airbus A350-900. Chicago becomes the carrier's eighth US city and its fifth on the US mainland.

The outbound flight, PR132, is scheduled to leave Manila at 4:40 p.m. and arrive in Chicago at 4:55 p.m. local time after a block time of 14 hours and 15 minutes. The return flight, PR133, departs Chicago at 10:45 p.m.; facing strong transpacific headwinds, it has a much longer block time of 16 hours and 40 minutes, arriving in Manila at 5:25 a.m. the next day, a morning arrival that suits onward connections. Philippine Airlines first announced the route in April, when it offered limited-time round-trip basic economy fares of $667 for bookings made until May 31. Cirium scheduling data shows the flights operating year-round, with a monthly peak of 14 departures in March 2027.

The route will use the carrier's 295-seat A350-900 in a three-class layout: 30 business, 24 premium economy and 241 economy seats, with nine seats per row in a 3-3-3 configuration in economy. Chicago joins Los Angeles, New York JFK, San Francisco and Seattle-Tacoma as the airline's mainland US destinations; it also serves Guam, Honolulu and Saipan, the last of these through its regional brand PAL Express. Philippine Airlines president Richard Nuttall said that "serving the Chicago–Manila corridor will create vital links to key regional destinations and major Philippine domestic markets through our Manila hub," adding that "Chicago is considered one of the premier hubs in the United States, and our entry into this vibrant city will provide direct connectivity to the Midwest."
